record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: Let Y be a smooth, strictly convex planar billiard table, let Φ be the phase space of its billiard map, let 𝒫⊂Φ be the set of all periodic points, and let 𝒫_n⊂Φ be the set of periodic points of period n. With respect to the invariant Liouville measure μ on Φ, is μ(𝒫)=0? Equivalently, is μ(𝒫_n)=0 for every n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth, strictly convex planar billiard table (a Birkhoff billiard), i.e. a compact planar region bounded by a smooth, strictly convex closed curve. The billiard map $T:\Phi\to\Phi$ acts on the phase space $\Phi$ consisting of pairs $(q,v)$, where $q$ is a boundary point and $v$ is an inward unit vector at $q$; $T$ sends $(q,v)$ to the next boundary impact point and post-reflection direction under the law of equal angles. The map $T$ preserves the Liouville measure $\mu$ on $\Phi$ (given, in arclength–angle coordinates $(s,\theta)$ with $\theta\in(0,\pi)$, by $d\mu = \sin\theta\,ds\,d\theta$).

Let $\mathcal{P}\subset\Phi$ denote the set of all periodic points of $T$, and for each integer $n\ge 2$ let $\mathcal{P}_n\subset\Phi$ denote the set of points of period $n$.

Prove or disprove:
(i) $\mu(\mathcal{P}) = 0$;
(ii) $\mu(\mathcal{P}_n) = 0$ for every $n\ge 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is Ivrii's conjecture on the measure of periodic billiard orbits. It is known to hold for periods $n=3$ (Rychlik and others) and $n=4$ (Glutsyuk–Kudryashov) in the planar case, and it is known for real-analytic strictly convex boundaries. For general smooth, strictly convex Birkhoff billiard tables and arbitrary period $n\ge 5$, the conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Ivrii's conjecture for some cases in outer and symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Ivrii's conjecture states that in every billiard in Euclidean space the set of periodic orbits has measure zero.

status_evidence.title: Billiard dynamics: An updated survey with the emphasis on open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 3 asks to prove μ(P)=0 and μ(P_n)=0 for any Birkhoff billiard table.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in the survey.

status_evidence.title: no planar billiard possesses an open set of quadrilateral orbits
status_evidence.snippet: Glutsyuk–Kudryashov: no planar billiard has an open set of 4-periodic orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Case n=4 is solved in the plane.
